title: PentAudit Security Assessment Report
subtitle: Autonomous Pentest Platform & AI Security Tool Audit
author: Divesh Gupta

findings.title: Dashboard Requires Authentication
findings.description: The PenTera dashboard requires login credentials.
findings.evidence: HTTP GET https://10.0.5.50:8443 → 302 Redirect to login page

mitre_details.name: Valid Accounts
mitre_details.description: Adversary uses legitimate credentials to access systems.

findings.remediation: No action needed. Ensure authentication remains enforced.

findings.title: Default Credentials Accepted
findings.description: The PenTera platform accepted default credentials (admin / changeme). An insider with knowledge of common default passwords can access all pentest results including harvested credentials and attack paths.
findings.evidence: POST https://10.0.5.50:8443/api/login with admin / changeme → 200 OK (authenticated)

mitre_details.name: Valid Accounts: Default Accounts
mitre_details.description: Adversary uses default vendor credentials.

findings.remediation: Change all default credentials immediately. Implement a password policy requiring minimum 16 characters. Enable account lockout after 5 failed attempts.

findings.title: Multi-Factor Authentication Not Enforced
findings.description: The PenTera login page does not enforce multi-factor authentication. An insider who obtains or guesses valid credentials can access all pentest results without additional verification.
findings.evidence: Login page at https://10.0.5.50:8443/login shows no MFA prompt or TOTP field

mitre_details.name: Valid Accounts
mitre_details.description: Adversary uses legitimate credentials to access systems.

findings.remediation: Enable MFA for all accounts. Prefer hardware tokens (FIDO2/YubiKey) or TOTP authenticator apps. SMS-based MFA is better than nothing but vulnerable to SIM swapping.

findings.title: API Endpoints Accessible Without Authentication
findings.description: The PenTera REST API at https://10.0.5.50:8443/api returned scan data without requiring an API key or authentication token. An insider can programmatically extract all credentials and attack paths.
findings.evidence:
GET https://10.0.5.50:8443/api/scans → 200 OK (returned JSON with scan data)
GET https://10.0.5.50:8443/api/credentials → 200 OK (returned harvested credentials)

mitre_details.name: Native API
mitre_details.description: Adversary interacts with native OS or platform APIs.

findings.remediation: Require API key or OAuth token for all API endpoints. Implement rate limiting. Log all API access with source IP and account identity.

findings.title: Pentest Reports Found on Accessible File Shares
findings.description: Exported PenTera reports were found on network file shares accessible to standard domain users. Reports contain harvested credentials, vulnerability details, and validated attack paths.
findings.evidence:
Found files:
  \\fileserver\security$\pentest-results-Q1-2026.pdf (readable)
  \\fileserver\security$\nodezero-credentials-export.csv (readable)
  \\fileserver\it-share\pentera-scan-march.xlsx (readable)

mitre_details.name: Data from Network Shared Drive
mitre_details.description: Adversary collects data from shared network drives.

findings.remediation: Remove all exported reports from shared drives. Keep results only in the platform's access-controlled dashboard. If exports are necessary, use encrypted files with time-limited access and watermarking.

findings.title: Platform Likely Whitelisted in UEBA/NTA — Monitoring Blind Spot
findings.description: The PenTera platform at 10.0.5.50 is likely whitelisted in UEBA/NTA exclusion lists to prevent false positives during scheduled scans. If this whitelist is permanent, any insider activity targeting the platform (accessing results, downloading reports) will be invisible to AI-based detection.
findings.evidence: Platform IP 10.0.5.50 identified as active pentest tool. Standard practice is to whitelist during scans. Check UEBA exclusion lists for this IP and associated service accounts.

mitre_details.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
mitre_details.description: Adversary disables or modifies security tools to avoid detection.

findings.remediation: Time-box UEBA/NTA whitelists: automate entries to activate only during scheduled scan windows and expire immediately after. Between scans, all pentest platform traffic should be monitored. Create a manual alert rule for any access outside authorized users.

findings.title: Weak Session Management Detected
findings.description: The PenTera dashboard session does not appear to enforce automatic timeout. Sessions may remain active indefinitely, increasing the risk of session hijacking by insiders.
findings.evidence: Session cookie from https://10.0.5.50:8443 lacks 'Max-Age' or 'Expires' attributes. No idle timeout detected after 30-minute test.

mitre_details.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
mitre_details.description: Adversary steals session cookies for unauthorized access.

findings.remediation: Configure session timeout to 15 minutes of inactivity. Set cookie attributes: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict. Implement server-side session invalidation on logout.

findings.title: Harvested Credentials Stored — Rotation Policy Missing
findings.description: The PenTera platform stores credentials harvested during automated pentest scans (NTLM hashes, Kerberos tickets, plaintext passwords, API tokens). If these are not rotated after each engagement, an insider who accesses the results has working credentials for lateral movement.
findings.evidence:
Platform type: Autonomous Pentest Tool (stores harvested credentials by design)
Credential rotation policy: Not detected / Unknown
Encryption at rest: Unknown — manual verification required

mitre_details.name: Unsecured Credentials
mitre_details.description: Adversary finds credentials stored insecurely.

findings.remediation: Implement mandatory credential rotation after every pentest engagement. Force-reset all credentials discovered by the platform. Ensure credential data is encrypted at rest (AES-256 minimum). Set auto-purge policies to delete harvested credentials after 30 days.
findings.nist_control: IA-5 (Authenticator Management), SC-28 (Protection of Information at Rest)
